verdict.tagline: A sprawling frontier sandbox severely hampered by rampant cheaters and technical friction.
for_you_if: you want a sprawling open world western sandbox
you enjoy slow paced frontier progression systems
not_for_you_if: you will not install a third party launcher
you are unwilling to encounter cheaters and modders
you expect active developer updates and new content

citations.review_text:
[h1][b]Greed Dead Online[/b][/h1]
I’m writing this in conjunction with my VERY positive RDR2 review just because I feel I need to get this off my chest. Ignore the number of hours it says I have, I've played this garbage for dozens of hours on my full copy of RDR2.

I like 100%ing games, which in my book means getting all the achievements on Steam. It’s my thing and I enjoy it, but every now and again that fixation of mine forces me to submerge myself in fecal matter such as this abysmal excuse for an online mode.

[h3]Unfinished story[/h3]
If you were excited to play this for its storyline or to further expand RDR2’s stellar universe then you’re ♥♥♥♥ out of luck. The story of this game mode, as half-assed as it was from what I’ve seen, was completely abandoned and unfinished in favor of R* other money printing machine; GTA5. 

[h3]♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ servers/dev support[/h3]
The servers suck ass and will kick you out of your session or change your session for seemingly no reason. This is common knowledge in the RDO community and is basically an accepted part of playing the game like “oh yeah the servers just do that sometimes, you get used to it.” This is not to mention that the devs do absolutely nothing to combat cheating, hacking, exploiting and the like. You are basically on your own. This brings me to my next point.

[h3]A community of griefers and exploiters[/h3]
This community of no-life having dweebs and cringe merchants have taken to using cheats and exploits to make other players miserable in a desperate attempt to find some kind of enjoyment or meaning in this piece of ♥♥♥♥ game mode that they have sunk so much time, effort and (most likely) money into. They will use the items and superior equipment they grinded for to bully new-comers and use exploits to lock them out of online mission completion. This comes in many forms but just as an example, players will kill you, steal the item/satchel you’re trying to deliver and hand it over to a non-interactable NPC. This b…
Filled with modders so you can't play the game. Peer to peer connection that sucks and barely works. A literal billion dollar company that can't afford dedicated servers. Not worth the time at all.

Horrible. DO NOT BUY THIS GAME.
The game itself is fantastic.
However, since the devs dropped regulations the ENTIRE community is polluted with nothing but hackers/modders who ruin the fun for vanilla players. They do nothing but crash your game and troll you the ENTIRE TIME.
Low life, no life, absolute losers who need to get a life.
Absolute waste of a beautiful game. Very sad to see it degraded to this state.
hacker infested garbage, but pretty fun when you are able to actually play the game.

Spend 67 Minutes in this game (including loadingtimes and adjusting settings) and already ran into a hacker with godmode who continued to hunt and kill me multiple times.

For a moment I forgot that Rockstar would look after their games.
Do not but RDO on it's own. The game has almost an unlimited amount of hackers/cheaters that Rockstar continues to ignore. Try to use a VPN when playing this if you do, hackers can get your IP. 2/10
it's a great game but it's a full of cheaters

Filled with cheaters and people using mod menu's, which break your ability to summon a horse, functionally ruining the multiplayer entirely, and being forced back into the same lobby without using change character to get a solo lobby temporarily just for a small amount of solace before the next person with mods breaks your ability to play again 10-15 mins later. 

honestly, I've played RDO on console for years, and this was genuinely unenjoyable with how often trash mobsters kept ruining the experience for dozens of people at a time.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that required third-party launcher and account sign-in procedures prevent them from playing or accessing the game.

citations.review_text:
It's like they went out of their way to design this in the most infuriating way possible
- Needs a separate launcher and account despite being available on steam
- Despite it not being the 80s, "spastic" and any possible variation of its spelling is considered a slur by this game, so I cant use my username
- It decides to ignore third party mouse software completely
- It disables the window key
- It's completely obnoxious trying to figure out how to friend people on it, cant just join a steam friend
- It's literally impossible to get my game's sensitivity right

Genuinely a terrible experience right off the bat

Who decided to make having a account a logical obstacle to play a game? They wont even allow you to make a new account to enter the game, it has to be a account you used before. If you want to play this game, I prefer you play it on the console to avoid this issue. Only a stupid person would program this. Sure its a good game but avoid PC for this main reason. Why in any world do this? Now you get a negative review for others to see. Don't get this game on the PC, this shouldn't even be a issue. They know I bought the game, its a video game not a verification process protocol. Fix this or this comment stays. I heard there is loads of hackers ruining the game from other comments so I guess its for the best. I just wanted to hunt with my creative character and relax, I guess I'll just do it on the console where I got the game for free. Next time plan ahead before you make a 5star game a 2star game because you wanted to add stupid protocols to play a game you already bought.

Genuinely garbage company.

I've had nothing but problems even trying to play this game. Their launcher and website were both throwing "#1.000.0" errors so I tried numerous fixes, including:

- VPN
- Mobile data
- Logging in on phone
- Deleting social club folder
- Restarting router
- Setting DNS settings to 8.8.8.8 / 8.8.4.4
- Flushing DNS settings and such via cmd prompt
- Checking my timezone / region are correct
- Restarting my laptop

Among others. I've been back and forth with their support all day trying to get it to work with their suggestions being less than helpful. They close the ticket and tell me to open an account recovery ticket, so I do so.

THEN they close it and block me from opening further tickets.

So I've got an unplayable game and an account I can't even access, whilst being blocked from support. 0/10 would NOT recommend, genuinely horrendous company with a clueless support team.

Edit: I managed to find the problem but their website and support team were still of little to no help.
i cannot actually get into my r* account so i naturally can’t ply it.

I bought the game and my whole playtime is entirely made up of me trying to log in or waiting for the game to load just for it to say "alert, you have been disconnected from rockstar servers" every single time I tried to log on, it didn't even finish loading before I was given this error. I tried everything to fix it, disconnecting and reconnecting to my network, downloading different versions of proton, and even connecting to my phone's hot spot but nothing worked. Already refunded, wouldn't recommend unless you know how to fix the issue.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe servers as overrun with hackers and cheaters who teleport, blow up players, and crash the game.

citations.review_text: Not worth playing when 70% of the time all they have in servers there are nothing but hackers being trolls or whatever the they want like invincibility. i just spawned in just to play and i am bombarded randomly with explode multiple times and somehow ♥♥♥♥♥♥ set to the enemy and i cant do anything but leave the game to reset server. This is ridiculous like i am not paying a $86.40 bounty i didn't make just cuz some worthless human being is using a skill to be a malicious. This whole experience is just disappointing and ridiculously frustrating that this is still an ongoing issue. i didn't ♥♥♥♥♥♥ pay money for a game that didn't work cuz i didn't have it on their launcher just to have to rebuy it and then have to deal with hackers.
beautiful game, but rife with hackers.

Pretty fun if a bit repetitive. The community is the only questionable aspect. like GTA 5 the game is infested with people who want nothing more than to ruin your experience and that is exacerbated by cheaters who will teleport directly to you and blow you up or set your honor as low as it can go. The mechanics on the other hand are clean and you get the quintessential Red Dead experience when things are going well.

I want to clarify in the beginning that you should not look at this game through the lense of online multiplayer. The "online" component of Red Dead Online is utter garbage. It is a well known fact that the game is overrun with hackers. Such characters can easily crash your game or worse. There is no adequate communication between players, the game doesn't support simple chat system, only voice. And even then, why would you communicate with anyone? Half of the players just grief your business deliveries or hunt you for the rest of the game unless you get away from them or bite back. The servers are dog ♥♥♥♥♥, you or your friends can easily lose connection or crash while waiting for a mission to load. For some strange reason, even after a successful job you may not get the payout, it happened to me a couple of times while playing with my friends. 

The partakable activities that the game can offer are not that engaging or fun either. For a time, sure, but they get old pretty quick.  Also, the grind for gold to unlock better roles is real, you gotta spend some time to unlock 3 of the most interesting roles (or have a friend that can launch and guide you through missions).

Where it does shine, is quote unquote singleplayer. RDO Lobby Manager allows you to host your own private lobby accessible only to you or your friends. With this installed, the game quickly turns into relaxing freeroam with meditative gameplay. RDO is a simple stub of RDR2, but it has couple advantages that make it a more preferable open-world game to me. You are allowed to go anywhere and everywhere from the start with your personal character you've created, no preset personality. You are not bound by any questline that forces you to move from one point of interest to the other. Hunt where you want, complete stupid radiant quests in any fashion you like, etc. In this regard, RDO is similar to STALKER Anomaly, GTA 5 Los Santos Red or M&B 1866 mod. It is pretty easy to sink lots of hours playing like…

The game is bug-ridden even after years of development; cheaters run wild while rockstar proceeds to show they don't give a ♥♥♥♥. Even when cheaters aren't ruining the game by blowing you up; killing you mid-mission; trapping you so you have to restart your game; and pulling you across the map from where you were- crashing your game, then the game itself will regularly disconnect you, crash on its own, and bug out causing you to lose furs while hunting for the trader role, fail missions and bounties regularly or die randomly; wasting funds and ammunition until you have to run free roam missions for scraps. The game is unpolished as hell and rockstar shows they don't give a damn what goes on in the game. Their "anti-cheat"- if it exists- is just as much of a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ joke as it always has been across their game franchises. It's a pathetic attempt at making a good game, but at least the missions are decently enjoyable and the story isn't bad so there are mild redeeming factors. Overall, however, it could be pretty fun if it wasn't bug-ridden and infested with petulant cheaters that make direct efforts to intentionally ruin your experience of the game every day you hop on regardless of how many times you reload the game or switch servers. The fact that the majority of any fun or better paying missions is locked behind a pay-or-grind wall makes it all that much worse. Any time that a mission is ruined, it could mean losing gold- the only ways to get it being through missions, usually only receiving .08 on average per mission, making it take days to achieve the ability to purchase licenses or kits that allow access to the majority of the game- or through purchasing gold in the store that only works 1/3 of the time at best. Massive disappointment Rockstar. Do better.

Hunt where you want, complete stupid radiant quests in any fashion you like, etc. In this regard, RDO is similar to STALKER Anomaly, GTA 5 Los Santos Red or M&B 1866 mod. It is pretty easy to sink lots of hours playing like…

The game is bug-ridden even after years of development; cheaters run wild while rockstar proceeds to show they don't give a ♥♥♥♥. Even when cheaters aren't ruining the game by blowing you up; killing you mid-mission; trapping you so you have to restart your game; and pulling you across the map from where you were- crashing your game, then the game itself will regularly disconnect you, crash on its own, and bug out causing you to lose furs while hunting for the trader role, fail missions and bounties regularly or die randomly; wasting funds and ammunition until you have to run free roam missions for scraps. The game is unpolished as hell and rockstar shows they don't give a damn what goes on in the game. Their "anti-cheat"- if it exists- is just as much of a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ joke as it always has been across their game franchises. It's a pathetic attempt at making a good game, but at least the missions are decently enjoyable and the story isn't bad so there are mild redeeming factors. Overall, however, it could be pretty fun if it wasn't bug-ridden and infested with petulant cheaters that make direct efforts to intentionally ruin your experience of the game every day you hop on regardless of how many times you reload the game or switch servers. The fact that the majority of any fun or better paying missions is locked behind a pay-or-grind wall makes it all that much worse. Any time that a mission is ruined, it could mean losing gold- the only ways to get it being through missions, usually only receiving .08 on average per mission, making it take days to achieve the ability to purchase licenses or kits that allow access to the majority of the game- or through purchasing gold in the store that only works 1/3 of the time at best. Massive disappointment Rockstar. Do better.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the developers have abandoned official updates for the online mode, leaving content static.

citations.review_text:
Official Inaction on Cheaters and Inadequate Anti-Cheat Measures (The Core Issue)
Despite widespread cheating, particularly on the PC version, the developers have taken virtually no fundamental action—such as issuing bans or implementing robust anti-cheat systems—effectively leaving the situation completely unchecked.
 The issue is so severe that switching sessions merely drops you into another server with cheaters, making a smooth gameplay experience impossible.
 In practice, players encounter cheaters roughly once every 10 minutes.


​Official Major Updates Have Effectively Ended
Because Rockstar Games has shifted its resources to other titles (such as GTA6), players can no longer expect significant new content additions or functional improvements moving forward.

​Stress from PK (Player Killing) and Griefing
Although defensive modes exist, players are still subject to unprovoked attacks or having their cargo stolen while traveling or completing missions.

After playing this game for over 200 hours, I would like to share my review. 

Unfortunately, the online version of Red Dead Redemption 2 has significant issues. 
The servers frequently crash, which results in the loss of progress, loot, mission data, and other. 

While the story mode of RDR2 is exceptional, with many engaging features, especially related to horses and camps, the online experience is quite disappointing. 
Taming wild horses in RDR2 Online does not allow you to bond with or sell them, they are essentially unusable. You cant remove the saddle and hitch your horse in your camp, like in the story mode, only certain breeds are viable for speed and health, and these breeds are costly, often requiring significant amounts of in game gold. 
The Arabian horse, valued at around 40 gold bars, is considered the best, but acquiring it can be pain.

Earning gold bars in RDR2 Online is difficult, due to the cheaters. 
Many lobbies are plagued with individuals who exploit the game by exploding players, teleporting, spawning zombies, or stealing from missions and other. 
Although stealing is part of the game, these cheaters are often untargetable or immune to damage, and they can crash your game or even your PC. 
Reporting these players does not lead to action, as Rockstar seems to overlook these for some reason.

I wish Rockstar would focus on resolving these problems by improving server stability, banning cheaters, and supporting a fair environment for regular players. 
Despite these issues, Rockstar has not reduced the prices for gold bars in their online shop, which I find surprising.

The story mode remains excellent, but playing online requires patience and hope that you will find a lobby free of cheaters. 
It’s unfortunate that a game that nearly won a Game of the Year award has been abandoned in terms of ongoing support and improvements.

I hope that someday Rockstar will update the game, fix the servers, ban cheaters, and introduce more story content and job…

i cant belive how dog his game is:(

a.) HACKERS: This game has rampant hackers playing with cheat codes which completely ruins the experience. Here are two examples (1) hackers randomly you are transported to 20 miles in the sky and you fall for 5 minutes until an untimely death. And it repeats itself every time you respawn [ie: you are spawned into the sky] (2) randomly you are dynamited with no one around you; when you respawn, you are dynamited immediately. In both scenarios you are stuck in an infinite loop until you quit the game. 

b.) No customer support. You submit a ticket and they immediately close the ticket and ask you to create the ticket the same way you did it the first time. 

c.) LAG! The game is hyper resource intensive for the poor graphics it provides and as a result, my GF and I have significant lag. We have played other higher quality graphics games such as Diablo and Destiny and never had a lag issue.

d.) BUGS unquipping you of weapons: Right before you start the hardest challenge of the game (Call to Arms), the game randomly unequips you from guns and equips you with stuff that can only stun animals (varmit rifle).  This happens 10% of the time. So not often enough that you commit to memory, but impactful enough to make you hate the game. Because you cannot start the game again for another 45 minutes. 

e.) Error codes galore! And they force you to quit the game and lose all progress

The game is amazing. Unfortunately, it's not worth playing. Had a blast playing it when it released. Took a hiatus and came back.
After loading in, i played a total of 15 minutes before uninstalling again. I was either being blown up, caged, or in general griefed by cheaters. The game isn't worth the frustration.
